No entry offer

Followers watch, then drift

Someone who connects with your reels on facilitation but isn’t ready for a retreat has nothing to sign up for. You can’t follow up with people you never captured.

No first purchase

A retreat is a big first yes

Travel, days away and a high-ticket price is a lot to ask of someone who found you this week. With nothing smaller to buy, most people buy nothing.

No qualifying step

You can’t see who is ready

There’s no class to show up to and no application to fill in, so the people who would say yes to a retreat look the same as everyone else scrolling.

Anyone not ready for a retreat today can follow you or join your group, but there is nothing to buy and no way to see who is ready.

Sound familiar?

You feel the calling. The room feels harder.

  • You’ve been asked to run something, and you’re not sure how to structure it.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 90 minutes

The custodian mindset

What it means to hold space as a custodian of the room, not a performer at the front of it.

Designing the arc of an event

How to plan the opening, the deepening and the closing so every gathering has a clear shape.

Holding the room when the energy shifts

Practical ways to stay grounded and steady when a group goes quiet, gets loud or stalls.

Agreements and boundaries

Simple intake questions and group agreements so everyone knows what they’re stepping into.

From one event to a calendar

How to plan your first or next gathering and invite the right people into it.

Script 1 · “The skill”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Holding space isn’t something you’re born with. It’s something you practise.”

Body

“The facilitators people come back to aren’t louder or more charismatic. They plan the shape of the event, they set clear agreements, and they know what to do when the room shifts. All of that can be learned.”

CTA

“I’m teaching it live in my Hold the Room masterclass. It’s $17 and the replay is included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera outdoors, natural light, slow push-in.

Script 2 · “The quiet room”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“What do you do when a whole group goes quiet?”

Body

“Most new facilitators rush to fill the silence. Often the better move is to slow down, name what’s happening and give the group one simple next step. I’ll show you exactly how I do that, plus the four other moments that make or break an event.”

CTA

“Live, 90 minutes, $17. Tap Sign up to save your seat.”

Shot: talking to camera, on-screen text “silence” highlighted in ember.

Script 3 · “The arc”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Every event people remember has the same three parts.”

Body

“An opening that helps people arrive. A middle that goes deeper. A close that lets them take something home. When one is missing, the event feels flat. When all three are there, people book the next one.”

CTA

“I’ll walk you through how to plan all three in my live masterclass. Seats are $17. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a simple drawn arc with the three parts labelled.
